scope: Native geometry evidence for the user-supplied ball-screw, miniature pinion, bevel-pair and jaw-coupling reference expansion.

runtime.execution: Headless local Python; temporary shapes and STEP files, without changing a user CAD document.

checks: Valid closed solids and expected component counts
Independent shaft bores and clear central shaft passage
Clamp screw through-holes and head counterbores on both hubs
Valid STEP round trips with retained solid counts
limits: Reference verifies D25, L30 and the listed bore pairs. Jaw, spider and clamp details are editable prototype dimensions.
Four bore combinations exercise boundary and mixed-bore geometry; this is not native validation of every possible custom parameter combination.

bevelPairs.scope: All assembly/separated states; both bore interval endpoints for each individual gear; linked 37 degree rotation.

checks: Valid closed positive-volume solids and expected component counts
All checked bevel assembly positions have zero measured component intersection
Valid STEP round trips with retained solid counts
gears.stepVolumeAcceptance: Absolute error < max(0.001 mm^3, native volume * 0.00001). Per-case STEP volume errors were asserted but not recorded; no measured maximum is claimed.
limits: Bevel teeth are faceted tapered layout approximations, not generated conjugate contact surfaces. Zero intersection at checked positions does not certify continuous meshing or load capacity.
Miniature spur width 5 mm, pressure angle 20 degrees and tooth thinning 0.02 mm are prototype assumptions. Low-tooth layout mode does not reproduce manufacturing undercut or profile shift.

ballScrews.codeVerification: The 135 retained non-cutaway generated Python bodies have unchanged geometry ASTs after excluding a defensive error guard. The final 131 cutaway bodies were rerun with the common 0.001 mm inspection offset. Per-case code hashes are recorded in the aggregate evidence.
ballScrews.algorithm: Elliptical groove profile seam shifted by 0.37 rad; direct nut-body groove cut; uniform +0.001 mm inspection-plane offset in preview and native CAD, with 0.00001 mm OCC common tolerance.
checks: Valid closed positive-volume components and expected retained solids
Preview/native envelope agreement for all 266 cases
Representative ball-to-housing race clearance samples in each nut configuration
Valid STEP round trips retaining solid counts
Exhaustive component-intersection checks on SFI1605 assembled and cutaway comparisons
ballScrews.stepVolumeAcceptance: The 266-case audit checks imported validity and solid counts. It does not claim a measured STEP volume error maximum.

independentShaftProbeDiagnostic.scope: Three full-shaft cases already included in the 266 native cases; these extra checks do not increase the unique case count.
independentShaftProbeDiagnostic.limitation: On the 550-turn SFK0401 shaft at z=165 mm, the full-shape OCC common query incorrectly returns the entire sphere despite positive shape separation, seven outside point samples, and zero intersection against a valid local shaft segment. That full-shape Boolean query is unreliable at this sample; it is not used as evidence of physical overlap.

limits: Catalog envelopes are transcribed dimensions, not certification of supplier interchangeability or load capacity. Undimensioned internal races, return paths, seals, tube routing and end machining remain editable prototype geometry.
Only the documented sample spheres and two exhaustive SFI1605 assemblies were tested for component contact; this is not a kinematic or load simulation.
A deterministic 0.001 mm inspection-plane offset avoids OCC degeneracies and is applied equally to preview and FreeCAD cutaways.
Two named options lacking complete dimensional evidence remain explicitly unverified prototype examples.
reproduce: Run scripts/verify-ball-screws.py with a FreeCAD Python runtime; see docs/ball-screw-catalog.md for commands.
